chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' said:

A man asked him about a man who died and left two brothers and a daughter, and the daughter was a minor. So one of the two brothers, the guardian, married the daughter to his son. Then the father of the married son (the one who performed the marriage) died. When he died, the other brother said: 'My brother did not marry his son,' so he married the girl to his son. It was said to the girl: 'Which of the two husbands is more dear to you, the first or the last?' She said: 'The last.' Then the second brother died, and the first brother had a son who was older than the married son. He said to the girl: 'Choose whichever is more dear to you, the first husband or the last husband.' He said: 'The narration regarding both is that she belongs to the last husband, and that is because she reached puberty when he married her, and she is not allowed to annul what she contracted after reaching puberty.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If the girl died before reaching puberty, the one to whom she was married did not inherit her. And if he died before her, his estate is not divided until the girl reaches puberty, then she swears that she did not consent to it for the sake of inheritance.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a minor girl's marriage if she reaches puberty versus if she dies before puberty?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of a minor girl's marriage (*nikah*) contracted by her guardian, emphasizing that upon reaching puberty, the marriage becomes binding and she cannot annul it merely by preferring a different suitor. It further distinguishes inheritance rights based on the timing of death: if she dies before puberty, the husband does not inherit her, whereas if he dies before she reaches puberty, she must swear she did not consent to the marriage for the sake of inheritance before the estate is divided. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view on the conditional validity of minor marriages and the specific evidentiary requirements for inheritance claims in such cases.
